A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLoRE study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, component ablations, sensitivity studies and representation analyses using Qwen and Llama models.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results, ablations and representation analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: GLoRE retains the same contrastive representation construction, domain-specific memory, cosine-similarity retrieval, normalization and first-/last-token injection procedures. The greedy-decoding statement is newly disclosed implementation information, not evidence of a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use STILL-2 examples from mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology, and evaluate on MATHOAI, AIME2024, AMC2023 and GPQA Diamond. No dataset, domain or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Zero-shot CoT, Few-shot CoT, BoostStep, MathNeuro, RoT and SFT. Figure 7 also retains the same larger-model comparators. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Removing v1 Appendix B.2 and Table 4 removes the four-condition control experiment crossing first- and last-token injection positions for the two components. Settings of retained experiments remain unchanged; the new greedy-decoding disclosure does not establish a decoding change.

E4.justification: The injection-position sensitivity study in v1 Appendix B.2 is removed. The memory-size and layer-selection studies from Appendices B.1 and B.3 are retained as v2 Sections 5.3.5 and 5.3.6, rather than newly added analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: v1 Table 4's alternative injection-position results disappear, including first/first accuracies of 74.40 on MATHOAI and 35.86 on GPQA. Retained benchmark tables, component-ablation scores and plotted results are unchanged; the default first/last scores remain reported elsewhere.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, including the representation operations and Appendix A's matrix-based entropy definition, remain unchanged. Table 3's complexity expressions and accompanying reasoning are also retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about general long-CoT capability, training-free representation engineering, and effectiveness and efficiency across domains.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and limitations concerning internal-model access and restricted experimental resources remain unchanged. Memory-size and layer-selection interpretations merely move into the main text; the removed injection-position passage reports a sensitivity finding rather than a distinct mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies greedy decoding for inference. Previously disclosed sample counts, injection strengths, retrieval count, model choices, baseline instructions and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Supporting citations expand, including ChainLM, DAWN-ICL, REAR and additional context-modeling and retrieval work. These additions leave the related-work narrative and the claimed distinction from short-CoT representation engineering essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: Two appendix subsections move into the main experimental analysis, subsequent subsections and appendices are renumbered, and acknowledgements are added. Other prose changes are limited; the central narrative is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is enlarged, the memory-size and layer-selection plots move into the main text, and v1 Table 4 is removed. The entropy figure and data-statistics table are renumbered. Retained graphics preserve their plotted content.

improvement.justification: Specifying greedy decoding improves reproducibility, and moving existing sensitivity studies into the main text makes them easier to find. However, removing v1 Appendix B.2 and Table 4 reduces empirical support for the token-injection choices. With the core method and remaining evidence unchanged, these limited benefits and losses do not establish a clear net quality direction.
